title: Priv EKS Control Plane Terraform: Staged Restore & Rollback Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an operational Terraform module and accompanying runbook to support safe staged restores and rollbacks for Redwood Private EKS control planes running in customer VPCs. This ticket covers: terraform idempotency patterns for restore workflows, state handling and locking (S3+Dynamo), snapshot orchestration for etcd/cluster state, post-restore health probes, automated rollback triggers, and operator playbook for on-call remediation. Goal: reduce Mean Time To Recovery (MTTR) for control plane incidents and provide a tested, documented path to restore to a known-good control plane state without manual state drift.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable Terraform module exists that can execute a staged control-plane restore with parameters for snapshot source, restore window, and dry-run mode
State locking and backup are validated (S3 bucket with DynamoDB lock table) and documented for cross-account KMS-encrypted state buckets
Automated health checks (control-plane readiness, API latency, kubelet join rate, etcd commit latency) run post-restore and emit alerts to the Console with runbook links
Rollback policy implemented: automatic rollback on critical SLO regressions OR manual rollback steps are documented and validated in a canary cluster
Playbook contains clear NOC steps, reconciliation commands, and safety checks (certificate re-issue, node re-join, kube-proxy roll reapply) validated in dry-run
End-to-end smoke test completes in the staging environment using infra-as-code pipeline and the results are recorded in the CI job (pass/fail artifacts attached)
steps: 1) Preflight: run terraform plan with -var-file=preflight.tfvars and preflight validator scripts (CIDR checks, KMS key access, S3 permissions)
2) Snapshot prepare: ensure latest etcd snapshot available in s3://redwood-priv-eks-snapshots/<cluster>/ with manifest.json and sha256
3) Lock state: acquire DynamoDB lock and create backup of current terraform state (timestamped copy) before any changes
4) Dry-run restore: terraform apply with restore.enabled=true and dry_run=true against a canary cluster in the same AZs
5) Post-restore probes: run /ops/health-checks/controlplane-checker.sh; verify API server 99th percentile latency < 200ms and etcd commit latency < 30ms

6) Canary validation: run workload-sim for 15 minutes, run regression eval prompts (chat generation) to verify inference path through Private deployment (if applicable), and collect cost/latency traces
7) Cutover: if canary passes, apply module with restore.enabled=false orchestrated via pipeline with step approvals, otherwise abort and run rollback steps

8) Rollback trigger: rollback automatically starts when monitoring fires critical alert or when manual 'rollback' flag is applied to the module variable; rollback re-applies the backed-up terraform state and signals the control-plane to use previous snapshot
9) Post-mortem: attach terraform plan/app logs, monitoring graphs, and timeline to the Confluence incident page and schedule follow-up retrofit tickets
